title.narrative: Supporting the Credit Guarantee System for Economic Diversification and Employment Project

description.narrative: The project aims to improve the access of Mongolia's small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to finance to sustain their businesses and thereby foster growth, diversify the economy, lessen its dependence on the mining sector, and create jobs. The TA will improve the quality of the Credit Guarantee Fund of Mongolia (CGFM) and the country's credit guarantee system. The government has asked the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to support commercial banks' lending to SMEs by backing CGFM credit guarantees. The project will expand the financing for SMEs in sectors not related to mining.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: A longer-term bank deposit market developed Indicator: At least four PFIs participating in the CGFM program regularly offer tugrik time deposits with maturities of at least 5 years by 2021 Achievement: 7 Progress/Status: Achieved. As of 31 December 2024, 7 PFIs in the CGFM program have offered 528 time deposits with maturities of at least 5 years amounting to a total of $53.5 million ($1 = MNT2,752.97). Data Source: Project monitoring reports; reports from the CGFM, PFIs, and the MOF

Output: Longer-term financing for SMEs increased Indicator: At least $57.13 million of funding is channeled to PFIs utilizing CGFM guarantees by end of 2026. (Baseline 2015: 0) (OP 1.2.1) Achievement: 180000 Progress/Status: Achieved. As of 31 December 2024, $72.9 million ($1 = MNT2,752.97) of funding has been channeled to PFIs from a total of $60 million drawdown from the Asian Development Bank. An amount of $12.9 million, exceeding the $60 million that was supposed to be withdrawn, was taken out of the escrow account and issued as a guaranteed loan. Data Source: Project monitoring reports; reports from the CGFM, PFIs, and the MOFALI reports

Output: Longer-term financing for SMEs increased Indicator: At least three new credit guarantee products are issued by CGFM with at least one supporting women entrepreneurs by end of 2022 (Baseline 2014: 0 new product) (OP 2.3.1) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. In July 2023, the CGFM collaborated with the Trade and Development Bank to launch the Green Guarantee Product. The following month, in August 2023, CGFM partnered with Capitron Bank to introduce a Women's Guarantee Product. In September 2023, CGFM collaborated with Trade and Development Bank once again to launch a guarantee product aimed at supporting SME exports. Additionally, on May 15, 2024, CGFM and Trade and Development Bank introduced the Guarantee Product for Supporting SMEs in the Agricultural Sector. Data Source: Project monitoring reports, CGFM reports

Output: Quality of the CGFM and the country's credit guarantee system improved Indicator: Two new procedures on risk management and financial management adopted and implemented by CGFM by end of 2018. (Baseline 2015: 2 old procedures) (OP 4.1.1) Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: Achieved. The new procedure for financial management was adopted and implemented by the board's resolution #22 on 25 April 2018. The procedure for risk management has been adopted and implemented by the board's resolution #33 on 14 August 2018. Updated on 25 February 2019. On 10 September 2022, the board's resolution #11 updated the risk management procedure. Data Source: Project monitoring reports; reports from the CGFM, MOFALI, and the MOI

Output: Quality of the CGFM and the country's credit guarantee system improved Indicator: . CGFM marketing program and action plan drafted and implemented jointly with regional CGFM representatives and PFIs by end of 2017. (Baseline 2015: none) (OP 4.2.2) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. The marketing plan is approved annually by the executive director. The 2025 marketing plan, included in CGFM's overall 2025 plan, was approved by the Board of Directors through an order issued on 26 December 2024. Data Source: Project monitoring report, CGFM Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Quality of the CGFM and the country's credit guarantee system improved Indicator: Amendments are adopted for enhancement of the legal framework supporting the credit guarantee system, including support for a private guarantee system by end of 2022. (Baseline 2015: 0) (OP 4.2.2) Achievement: N Progress/Status: Partially achieved. A draft law proposing amendments to the Law on the CGFM was prepared and internally reviewed, the government did not adopt the required amendments by end 2016 as targeted. Subsequent amendments to the CGFM Law were adopted in 2021 and 2024, addressing mortgage loan advance payment guarantees and loan guarantees for herders' cooperatives, respectively. In total, four working groups were established to address the Law on the CGFM, with amendments made on two occasions. Data Source: Project monitoring reports; reports from the CGFM, MOFALI, and the MOI Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2022 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Quality of the CGFM and the country's credit guarantee system improved Indicator: Management information system of CGFM allows collecting, reporting and analyzing of gender disaggregated data on the number of guarantees and loans issued, types and sizes of loans, and repayment status of loans by end of 2018. (Baseline 2015: no data) (OP 2.4.1) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved.On 5 November 2018, CGFM acquired the “NES” program from Grape City LLC. However, due to non-compliance, a contract was signed for the purchase of a new program from Erdenes Solutions LLC, and it is currently undergoing testing and improvement. The CGFM is also collaborating with the Korean the Korea Credit Guarantee Fund (KODIT) and the Japanese JPG guarantee funds to digitize CGFM's operations and empower the staff involved in this digital transformation.
Data Source: Project monitoring report, CGFM Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Mix of rural vs. urban area SME loan accounts opened increases to 20% (Baseline 2011: 17.3%) (OP 1.1) Achievement: 25.0 Progress/Status: Achieved. Rural SME loan accounts opened is 27.5% of the total opened. In 2024, CGFM opened four branches in the region, resulting in an increase in the local guarantee amount. Data Source: Global Financial Inclusion Database (World Bank: Annual)

SME loan accounts opened by women SMEs account for half of total SME loan accounts opened (Baseline 2014: 46%) (OP 2.4) Achievement: 49.1 Progress/Status: Achieved. Loan accounts opened by SMEs run by women account for 51.1% of all SME loan accounts opened within the project. Data Source: PFI reports

Number of active enterprises with fewer than 50 employees increase at a 10% annual average rate during 2016-2022 (Baseline 2014: 8.8% average annual rate of increase from 2006 to 2014) (OP 1.2) Achievement: 10 Progress/Status: Achieved. Share of newly approved enterprises under the program with fewer than 50 employees reached 96.2% in 2025 and an average of also 96.2% over 2017-2025; Share of active enterprises under the program with fewer than 50 employees reached 94.2% in 2025 and an average of 95.8% over 2017-2025. Average growth rate of active enterprises under the program with fewer than 50 employees is 15.4% over 2019-2025. Data Source: Global Financial Inclusion Database (World Bank: Annual) and Mongolian Year Book (NSO: Annual)
